old_caption: A mousetrap rests on a textured surface against a brick wall. A hand is partially visible on the left side of the frame. The trap's wooden base and metal spring mechanism are visible, with the trap in a set position. The trap remains stationary throughout the sequence, with no movement or action occurring. The lighting is dim and consistent, highlighting the trap and the surface texture. No animals or additional characters are visible in the frame.
original_wisa_caption: The video begins with a close-up shot of a hand holding a mousetrap. The hand is positioned above a metal surface, which appears to be part of a workbench or similar industrial setting. In the background, there is a brick wall, adding an urban or workshop ambiance to the scene. The hand then releases the mousetrap, which falls onto the metal surface. The mousetrap lands with its spring mechanism fully extended, indicating it has been set. The video captures the mousetrap in various stages of landing and settling on the metal surface, emphasizing the mechanical action and the contrast between the wooden trap and the metallic backdrop. There are no visible animals or additional characters in the frame, focusing solely on the mousetrap and its interaction with the environment. The lighting is consistent throughout, highlighting the details of the mousetrap and the texture of the metal surface.
caption: A wooden snap-trap base rests on a dark textured mat before a reddish brick wall, its copper kill-bar lying flat across the board. Balanced atop the bar's wire loop is a smaller wooden lever tipped with a yellow clip, propped at a steep upward angle. At the left edge a person's fingers appear briefly, then withdraw and leave the frame within the first moments. As the hand disappears, the small lever begins a slow descent, its raised yellow end tilting downward toward a near-horizontal position. The trap base itself stays fixed on the surface throughout. Over the latter portion of the clip the copper kill-bar gradually swings upward from its flat position, rising into a tall, near-vertical orientation. These rotations proceed slowly and continuously, with no sudden snap or impact visible. The brick background and mat texture remain unchanged as the mechanism reconfigures.
